diagram_math_checks.justification: Both left objects are B×Σ and both right objects are Ω. For each fixed g∈G, Φ(g) acts on B×Σ by L2 and def-imprimitive-wreath-product-of-permutation-groups; g acts on Ω by the given action. Each horizontal map is Ψ(b,C)=t_C·b, landing in C⊆Ω since t_C B=C.

diagram_math_checks.check: Block partition and inverse of Ψ
diagram_math_checks.justification: By def-block-and-block-system-for-a-group-action, two translates of B are equal or disjoint: apply the block condition to h^{-1}g. Transitivity covers Ω by the translates. Therefore ω lies in a unique C, and t_C^{-1}·ω lies in B; (t_C^{-1}·ω,C) is the unique inverse image. No additional choice is introduced beyond the representatives already chosen in the Statement.

diagram_math_checks.check: Inverse block-index and wreath multiplication convention
diagram_math_checks.justification: The local wreath definition specifies (k·f)(D)=f(k^{-1}·D) and (f,k)(f′,k′)=(f(k·f′),kk′). Since k_g(C)=g·C, the product component is f_g(D) f_h(g^{-1}·D), matching step 2.1 and the cancellation t_{g^{-1}D}t_{g^{-1}D}^{-1}. Its action is (f,k)·(b,C)=(f(k·C)·b,k·C), hence the left arrow really uses f_g(g·C), not f_g(C).

Both horizontal arrows point right; both action arrows point down. Step 1.1 with D=g·C gives f_g(g·C) induced by t_{g·C}^{-1}gt_C∈G_B. Down then right gives t_{g·C}·(f_g(g·C)·b)=g·(t_C·b), identical to right then down by step 3.1. These are the only asserted square relations.
The complete four-step proof is unchanged and ends before Remarks; the new square only depicts its existing step 3.1 identity.
